definitions.gloss: letter; written document; formal written communication
definitions.explanation: A formal or official written communication, especially a letter. Often used in historical or formal contexts, as well as in legal and diplomatic settings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{抗議|こうぎ}→抗議：12807_kougi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{書状|しょじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: To send a letter of protest.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大統領|だいとうりょう}→大統領：03418_daitouryou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{書状|しょじょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}いた→届く：00899_todoku⟧。
examples.english: A letter arrived from the president.

examples.japanese: ⟦{博物館|はくぶつかん}→博物館：01494_hakubutsukan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}→戦国時代：19200_sengokujidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{武将|ぶしょう}→武将：13222_bushou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧{書状|しょじょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{展示|てんじ}→展示：12401_tenji⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A letter written by a warlord from the Sengoku period is on display at the museum.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{書|しょ}→〜書：28467_sho⟧ (writing, document) + ⟦{状|じょう}→状：09878_jou⟧ (form, letter). A formal word for written correspondence, contrasting with the everyday word ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書状|しょじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧: to send a letter
- ⟦{抗議|こうぎ}→抗議：12807_kougi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{書状|しょじょう}: letter of protest
- ⟦{公開|こうかい}→公開：11665_koukai⟧{書状|しょじょう}: open letter
- {書状|しょじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{認|したた}める: to pen a letter (literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧: letter — the everyday word for a letter; informal and neutral
- ⟦{書簡|しょかん}→書簡：20091_shokan⟧: correspondence, letter — equally formal; used in literary and academic contexts
- ⟦{文書|ぶんしょ}→文書：12947_bunsho⟧: document, written text — broader; covers official documents, not just letters
- {親書|しんしょ}: personal letter (from a head of state) — specifically a diplomatic letter between leaders

USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in historical, legal, and diplomatic contexts. In everyday life, ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧ is the normal word for a letter. {書状|しょじょう} adds formality and gravity, suggesting an important or official communication.
